text:
Predicates:
ListedInYelp(x) ::: x is listed in Yelp's recommendations.
HasManyNegativeReviews(x) ::: x has received many negative reviews.
RatingGreaterThanFour(x) ::: x has a rating greater than four.
ProvidesTakeOut(x) ::: x provides take-out service.
PopularAmongLocals(x) ::: x is popular among local residents.
Store(x) ::: x is a store.

Premises:
∀x (ListedInYelp(x) → ¬HasManyNegativeReviews(x)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp's recommendations, then it has not received many negative reviews.
∀x (Rating(x) > 4 → ListedInYelp(x)) ::: All restaurants with a rating greater than four are listed in Yelp's recommendations.
∃x (¬ProvidesTakeOut(x) ∧ HasManyNegativeReviews(x)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀x (PopularAmongLocals(x) → Rating(x) > 4) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than four.
Rating(HamdenSubway) > 4 ∨ PopularAmongLocals(HamdenSubway) ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store has a rating greater than four, or it is popular among local residents.

Conclusion:
(ProvidesTakeOut(HamdenSubway) ∧ HasManyNegativeReviews(HamdenSubway)) → (Rating(HamdenSubway) > 4 ∧ ¬ProvidesTakeOut(HamdenSubway)))
